notes.PURPOSE: The public testnet of docs/decisions/testnet-measurements.md. It exists to produce the numbers that file says are unmeasured, so it deviates from spec/params.json in SIX values and nowhere else. Every other parameter is byte-identical to mainnet on purpose: a testnet that differs from the network it is rehearsing measures its own economics rather than mainnet's, and the reorg-depth distribution, the base-fee behaviour and the emission curve are exactly what will not transfer if the block time, the epoch length or the gas schedule are 'made convenient' here. Read the mainnet file for what every unchanged parameter means; this file only explains what moved.
notes.name: A different name is a different parameter file is a different consensus root is a different genesis id, and the genesis id IS the network id (R3-1). So testnet and mainnet nodes disconnect at the handshake, before a block is evaluated, and testnet coins can never be mined onto mainnet. That is structural, not a filter.
notes.chain_id: 2, allocated in spec/chain-ids.json and distinct from mainnet's 1. The testnet carries mainnet's consensus rules under its own id, so a certificate signed for one is refused on the other twice over: V1 compares the declared chain id, and the signing preimage binds it as well (core/crypto.SigningMessage). An id is allocated once and never reused as a rule, and this network is the one standing exception to it: the 2026-09-04 respin kept id 2 under spec/chain-ids.json's THE_PRE_MAINNET_RESPIN_EXCEPTION, which applies only before mainnet launches, only when the respin moves a consensus value so the consensus root moves with it, and only when the old incarnation is gone. Read that entry before copying the pattern -- it does NOT extend to mainnet. The id is also folded into the proof-of-work key -- pow.KeyFor derives from height AND chain id -- so testnet and mainnet never share a RandomX key even at the same height.
notes.pow_engine: randomx-v2, the same work function as mainnet, which requires `make build-randomx`. This network is BORN on rx/2 rather than forking onto it: there is no height gate and no activation, because it has not launched yet and a pre-genesis network can simply start on the function it means to run. rx/2 is selected by RANDOMX_FLAG_V2 on the vendored library, which computes both functions from one build and allocates exactly the same memory for either. A dev-blake3 testnet would be cheaper to run and would measure nothing about the thing this network exists to measure: real proof of work, real key rotation, and the memory a verifying node actually needs. A binary built without the randomx tag refuses to start against this file rather than falling back to the development engine.
notes.genesis_target: 2^246, versus mainnet's 2^238. NOT a relaxed rule -- it is where the difficulty rule STARTS, and the LWMA moves it from there within difficulty_window blocks. Mainnet's value assumes a launch hashrate that a testnet does not have on day one, and starting a chain 256x above its own hashrate means the first blocks arrive hours apart while the retarget crawls toward reality at difficulty_clamp_factor per block. 2^246 is about 1024 expected hashes per block, which a single small VPS solves in seconds, so the chain moves from block 0 and the rule -- not the seed -- decides the difficulty from then on.
notes.max_target: 2^252: 64x of headroom above this genesis_target, against mainnet's 4096x above its own. BlockWork at the ceiling is floor(2^256 / (2^252 + 1)) = 15, so a header at the easiest permitted difficulty still costs about 16 expected hashes and block work stays a four-bit measurement rather than a bit. The headroom matters MORE on a testnet than on mainnet in one specific way: testnet hashrate is volunteered and can collapse to zero when people switch machines off, which is precisely the excursion this ceiling has to absorb without the target walking to where every hash is a valid header.
notes.genesis_time: 1788501600 (2026-09-04T06:00:00Z), the relaunch hour, and a round UTC value as docs/RELEASE.md section 2 requires. It is set to the day the network is stood up rather than to any earlier date, and that is not cosmetic: the LWMA reads the gap between a block's timestamp and its parent's, so a genesis dated well before block 1 is mined presents the rule with one enormous solve time and it responds by clamping the target upward for several blocks. Harmless and self-correcting, but it means the first blocks measure the parameter file's date rather than the network. It is an HOUR rather than a date because the network is being stood up immediately rather than scheduled: the encoding work it was waiting on is merged, so the reason to wait is gone. The value is still a round UTC hour, as docs/RELEASE.md section 2 requires. It clears the freeze constraint with room to spare -- docs/GENESIS-CHECKLIST.md section 1.4 targets 2026-09-12 and requires every consensus-visible encoding change to be RUNNING on the relaunched network by then, and the relaunch milestone is due 2026-09-10 -- because launching earlier can only lengthen the soak, never shorten it. Move this to the new launch day if the network is ever reset from genesis. The first incarnation ran from 1788048000 (2026-08-30T00:00:00Z) and was invalidated by the proof-of-work blob reshape, which is a consensus change no chain can be continued across. This value was then held at a scheduled 2026-09-06 while that work landed, and brought forward to the hour above once it had: a pre-genesis network gains nothing by waiting, and every day it does not run is a day the measurements it exists to produce are not being taken. The id did NOT move with it -- see the chain_id note above and the ledger entry it points at.
notes.randomx_key_interval: 512 with the same 64-block lag, against mainnet's 2048/64. At a 30 s block that is a re-key roughly every 4.2 hours instead of every 17, so the boundary is crossed about six times a day by ordinary operation instead of once. THE BOUNDARY IS THE THING TO MEASURE: a mining node rebuilds the ~2 GiB dataset there and verifies NOTHING while it does (docs/RUNNING.md), and the length of that pause on real hardware under real load is a number no lab run has produced. The lag stays at an eighth of the interval, the ratio devnet also keeps, and Validate requires it strictly below the interval.
notes.undo_depth: UNCHANGED at mainnet's 1024, and this is the single most important thing in this file. It is §1 of testnet-measurements.md -- irreversible at genesis, a wrong value is a permanent partition boundary rather than a margin -- and the lab measurement of the reorg-depth tail is right-censored at whatever value is configured. Lowering it here to save disk would censor the sample at the new value and destroy the measurement this network was built to take.
notes.coinbase_maturity: UNCHANGED at 100. This chain has no premine and no faucet: for roughly the first hundred blocks only miners can transact, and that ramp is part of what a public testnet is supposed to rehearse.
notes.target_block_seconds: UNCHANGED at 30. Every time-denominated observation the testnet produces -- reorg depth, propagation, base-fee response, the key-rotation pause as a fraction of block time -- is a function of this. A faster testnet is a different regime, and regime is exactly what testnet-measurements.md says does not transfer.
